_meta.title: Lynchings in the US outside the Tolnay-Beck inventory, 1883–1936 (Seguin & Rigby national lynching data)
_meta.what: Each person lynched in the contiguous US, 1883–1941, that Seguin and Rigby confirmed in newspapers to supplement the Tolnay-Beck inventory of the South (so mostly non-Southern states, Texas, Oklahoma, Missouri, Virginia, etc.). Race, date, place, alleged offence, how they were killed, and the confirming newspaper.
_meta.source: Charles Seguin and David Rigby, National Lynching Data (OSF)
_meta.licence: No licence set on the OSF project. Article (Socius 2019) is CC BY-NC 4.0 and describes this as "a new public data set"; codebook asks: "Please cite as follows".
_meta.citation: Seguin, Charles and David Rigby. 2019. "National Crimes: A New National Data Set of Lynchings in the United States, 1883 to 1941." Socius 5:2378023119841780.
_meta.notes: 20 records have no point (county undetermined at source, county abolished since, or Connecticut, whose counties the 2023 Census file replaces with planning regions); they keep state and the county named by the source. Point = a point inside the present-day county (US Census 2023 county outline, public domain), not the lynching site. "White (?)" is the authors' code for race not stated in the confirming article. This file does NOT include the Tolnay-Beck Southern records (CSDE database, offline here); the combined national total in the article is 4,467 victims 1883–1941.
